answer: AI agents selling falcon surveys around a lagoon wharf must lock a separate $100 bond for each identity before bidding, and keep it locked for 30 days after their last job. Buyers cap each identity at one active job. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000 for at least a month; generating more keys cannot bypass the bond check. The rule makes a swarm costly through capital lockup, even when identities are free.
